purpose: Evaluate natural-query retrieval and later compare manual query rewriting on a separate exploratory challenge set.

limitations: Queries were authored with knowledge of source content.
This is not a blind or independently annotated benchmark.
Results should not be generalized to all real-world queries.
EPA guidance is US-centric and does not replace local German rules.

cases.natural_query: After unpacking groceries and deliveries, how can I tell which paper-based packaging is ready for the recycling bin?
A takeaway meal came in a paper container, and a shipping box has food marks on it. What should I check or do before putting either item out?
Do paper packaging and boxes need the same preparation, and what should I do if food is still attached?
When sorting empty jars at home, how should I deal with their closures and any glass that has shattered?
Several bottles are empty, but one drinking glass has broken. Can all of them go into the same collection container?
What should I know about sorting different kinds of glass, and what safety issue arises when an item is already broken?
I have reusable food tubs that are no longer needed for food. How should I prepare them for collection?
A container still smells of yesterday's dinner and has sauce around the edges. What should I do before sorting it?
How do I decide whether a food container is accepted locally, and what condition should it be in when I put it out?
What should I do with empty beverage packaging made from aluminum, including thin wrapping material?
I am about to sort drink containers, their metal closures, and a sheet of kitchen wrapping. Are there any preparation steps or separation rules I should know?
Can metal food and drink packaging be recycled with residue still attached, and does changing its shape help sorting?
Some small power cells from household gadgets are spent. How can I find an appropriate route for handing them over?
I am clearing out a drawer containing batteries from a remote, a camera, and a rechargeable gadget. Can they all go in ordinary household waste?
Does the type of battery affect where it should be handed in, and which collection options are described for household use?
My old phone and television are taking up space. What options are available for passing them on responsibly?
A small household gadget has stopped working. Is the normal curbside collection route suitable, or should I look elsewhere?
Where could unwanted consumer devices be handed over, and which kinds of organizations may offer collection options?
I am sorting my wardrobe and some footwear. How should I decide what can be passed on and what needs another route?
A charity might accept my old clothes, but some items are torn and a pair of shoes is badly damaged. What should I check?
What alternatives to throwing away unwanted garments and shoes are mentioned, and how does their condition affect the next step?
